system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Hong Kong, China. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Hong Kong itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Hong Kong space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Central/Soho, Sheung Wan/Sai Ying Pun, Wan Chai/Causeway Bay, Wong Chuk Hang/Aberdeen, Chai Wan/Eastern, Tsim Sha Tsui/Kowloon) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Hong Kong spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Hong Kong, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Gagosian
galleries.note: The first blue-chip mega-gallery to plant a flag in Hong Kong (2011), its Pedder Building space set the template for the city's international gallery scene and still stages museum-calibre shows.

galleries.name: David Zwirner
galleries.note: Anchor tenant of H Queen's since 2018, bringing Wolfgang Tillmans, Yayoi Kusama and Michaël Borremans to Asia and driving the market's centre of gravity toward Hong Kong.

galleries.name: Hauser & Wirth
galleries.note: Two-floor flagship with an ambitious estates and historical programme (Louise Bourgeois, Philip Guston) plus strong Asian artist representation and education programming.

galleries.name: White Cube
galleries.note: In Hong Kong since 2012; a street-level space that gave the city early exposure to the YBAs and now to Tracey Emin, Antony Gormley and Asian names such as Zhou Li.

galleries.name: Pace Gallery
galleries.note: A pioneer of the Asia market with deep Chinese contemporary ties (Zhang Xiaogang, Yoshitomo Nara) and a strong record with teamLab and light/technology art.

galleries.name: Perrotin
galleries.address_hint: K11 ATELIER Victoria Dockside, 18 Salisbury Road
galleries.note: Opened 2012 and later moved across the harbour; a key conduit for Murakami, JR, Daniel Arsham and emerging Asian artists with strong fair presence.

galleries.name: Para Site
galleries.address_hint: 22/F Wing Wah Industrial Building, 677 King's Road
galleries.note: Hong Kong's oldest and most internationally respected independent art space (founded 1996); its exhibitions, conferences and residencies shape curatorial discourse across Asia.

galleries.name: Tai Kwun Contemporary
galleries.note: Non-collecting kunsthalle inside the former Central Police Station compound; its large-scale thematic exhibitions and performance programme are the city's critical benchmark.

galleries.name: Lehmann Maupin
galleries.note: Long-standing Asia presence championing Do Ho Suh, Lee Bul, Nari Ward and Tammy Nguyen; consistently strong institutional placements from Hong Kong.

galleries.name: Massimo De Carlo
galleries.note: Rem Koolhaas-designed Pedder Building space since 2016, presenting European conceptual and painting positions alongside Asian debuts.

galleries.name: Blindspot Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 15/F Po Chai Industrial Building, 28 Wong Chuk Hang Road
galleries.note: The city's leading gallery for photography and lens-based work, with a rigorous Hong Kong and Chinese roster (South Ho, Trevor Yeung, Zhang Xiao) and strong institutional traction.

galleries.name: Kiang Malingue
galleries.note: Formerly Edouard Malingue; the most globally visible Hong Kong-founded gallery, representing Samson Young, Ho Tzu Nyen, Wong Ping and Tromarama with a biennial-heavy roster.

galleries.name: Hanart TZ Gallery
galleries.note: Johnson Chang's gallery, founded 1983, effectively introduced Chinese contemporary art to the world through the 1993 'China's New Art, Post-1989' exhibition.

galleries.name: Empty Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 18-19/F Grand Marine Center, 3 Yue Fung Street, Tin Wan
galleries.note: Black-box gallery devoted to time-based, sound and moving-image practices; its research-driven programme (Takashi Makino, Tishan Hsu, Aki Onda) has outsized critical standing.

galleries.name: de Sarthe
galleries.address_hint: 20/F Global Trade Square, 21 Wong Chuk Hang Road
galleries.note: Family gallery that shifted from modern masters to experimental young Chinese artists; a pioneer of the Wong Chuk Hang gallery cluster.

galleries.name: Tang Contemporary Art
galleries.note: Major Beijing-founded gallery whose Hong Kong space shows leading Chinese and Southeast Asian artists including Ai Weiwei, Wang Du and Zhao Zhao.

galleries.name: Ben Brown Fine Arts
galleries.note: Early arrival (2009) in the Pedder Building; blends postwar European masters with contemporary names such as Awol Erizku and Vik Muniz.

galleries.name: Pearl Lam Galleries
galleries.note: Influential cross-cultural programme linking Chinese abstraction, design and Western artists; a fixture of Hong Kong's fair and social art scene since 2012.

galleries.name: Almine Rech
galleries.note: Asian outpost of the Paris/Brussels gallery, showing Picasso estate material alongside contemporary painters with strong regional collector demand.

galleries.name: Axel Vervoordt Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 21/F Coda Designer Centre, 62 Wong Chuk Hang Road
galleries.note: Brings the Belgian dealer's Zero, Gutai and material-based sensibility to Asia; a major draw for the Wong Chuk Hang district.

galleries.name: Asia Art Archive
galleries.note: The region's essential research library and public programme platform; its displays, residencies and commissions underpin scholarship on Asian contemporary art.

galleries.name: Galerie Ora-Ora
galleries.note: Hong Kong-founded gallery known for ink-informed contemporary practice and paper-based work, active in fair leadership and gallery-association advocacy.

galleries.name: Rossi & Rossi
galleries.address_hint: 3C Yally Industrial Building, 6 Yip Fat Street
galleries.note: London-founded dealer of Himalayan and Asian art turned champion of contemporary Tibetan, Mongolian and South Asian artists.

galleries.name: 10 Chancery Lane Gallery
galleries.note: Katie de Tilly's gallery, open since 2001, with a socially engaged programme spanning Cambodia, Vietnam and Hong Kong and a long-running Chai Wan project space history.

galleries.name: Gallery Exit
galleries.address_hint: 3/F Blue Box Factory Building, 25 Hing Wo Street, Tin Wan
galleries.note: Consistent supporter of Hong Kong painters and conceptual artists since 2008; a reliable barometer of local emerging practice.

galleries.name: Whitestone Gallery
galleries.note: Tokyo gallery whose two-floor Hong Kong flagship anchors Gutai and postwar Japanese art in the city, alongside contemporary Asian names.

galleries.name: Osage Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 4/F Union Hing Yip Factory Building, 20 Hing Yip Street
galleries.note: Large industrial-space gallery with a quasi-institutional, research-led programme on Asian contemporary art and an associated foundation.

galleries.name: Ota Fine Arts
galleries.note: Tokyo gallery known for Yayoi Kusama and Southeast Asian artists such as Tang Da Wu and Chim↑Pom; a key Japanese presence in Hong Kong.

galleries.name: Galerie du Monde
galleries.note: One of Hong Kong's oldest galleries (1974), bridging Chinese modern ink masters and contemporary abstraction.

galleries.name: Kwai Fung Hin Art Gallery
galleries.note: Long-established Central gallery pairing European modern names with Chinese contemporary artists such as Zhou Chunya and Ju Ming.

galleries.name: Alisan Fine Arts
galleries.address_hint: Hing Wai Centre, 7 Tin Wan Praya Road
galleries.note: Founded 1981 by Alice King; the pioneering dealer of the New Ink movement and Chinese-diaspora modernists, with a second Central space.

galleries.name: Contemporary by Angela Li
galleries.note: Hollywood Road mainstay since 2008 showing Chinese and Hong Kong mid-career artists with a strong photography and painting mix.

galleries.name: Over the Influence
galleries.note: Multi-floor gallery driving the street-art-adjacent and figurative contemporary market in Asia, with a young international collector base.

galleries.name: WOAW Gallery
galleries.note: Fast-growing homegrown gallery with several Hong Kong locations, known for pop-inflected and emerging international artists and sell-out fair booths.

galleries.name: Villepin
galleries.note: Founded by Dominique and Arthur de Villepin; a collector-driven space with slow, single-artist exhibitions (Zao Wou-Ki, Fu Baoshi) and strong programming ambition.

galleries.name: PHD Group
galleries.note: Young curatorially minded gallery co-founded by Willem Molesworth and Ysabelle Cheung; noted for experimental shows and its role in reviving discursive energy in the local scene.

galleries.name: Karin Weber Gallery
galleries.note: Soho fixture since 2000 supporting Hong Kong and Southeast Asian emerging artists through residencies and long-term relationships.

galleries.name: Grotto Fine Art
galleries.note: Founded by Henry Au-yeung, the most consistent advocate for Hong Kong-born artists and local art history over more than two decades.

galleries.name: Hong Kong Arts Centre
galleries.note: Since 1977 the city's central independent arts institution; the Pao Galleries and its film/media programmes have incubated generations of local artists.

galleries.name: Videotage
galleries.address_hint: Unit 13, Cattle Depot Artist Village, 63 Ma Tau Kok Road
galleries.note: Artist-run collective founded 1986; the definitive Hong Kong platform for video, media and now blockchain-related art.

galleries.name: 1a space
galleries.address_hint: Unit 14, Cattle Depot Artist Village, 63 Ma Tau Kok Road
galleries.note: Artist-run non-profit since 1998 known for experimental, locally rooted and socially critical exhibitions at the Cattle Depot.

galleries.name: Oi!
galleries.note: Government-run heritage art space with a community and experimental focus; a key incubator for young Hong Kong artists and public-art projects.

galleries.name: CHAT (Centre for Heritage, Arts and Textile)
galleries.address_hint: The Mills, 45 Pak Tin Par Street
galleries.note: Non-profit art centre in a converted cotton mill commissioning ambitious textile-related contemporary art and international collaborations.

galleries.name: Asia Society Hong Kong Center
galleries.note: Non-collecting gallery in a landmark Tadao Ando-adjacent heritage site, presenting scholarly exhibitions of Asian modern and contemporary art.

galleries.name: K11 Art Foundation
galleries.address_hint: chi K11 art space, Victoria Dockside, 18 Salisbury Road
galleries.note: Adrian Cheng's foundation and its public art spaces have funded major museum collaborations and given many Chinese artists their first large platforms.

galleries.name: Sin Sin Fine Art
galleries.note: Long-running gallery with a distinctive focus on Indonesian and Southeast Asian contemporary artists.

galleries.name: 3812 Gallery
galleries.note: Hong Kong-founded gallery promoting 'Eastern Origin' contemporary Chinese art, with a London branch and steady fair presence.

galleries.name: Puerta Roja
galleries.note: The city's specialist in Latin American and Spanish contemporary art, an unusual and well-curated counterweight to the Asia-focused scene.

galleries.name: Soluna Fine Art
galleries.note: Focused on Nordic and Asian craft-based contemporary art, with a strong ceramics and material-culture programme.

galleries.name: Blue Lotus Gallery
galleries.note: Dedicated photography gallery documenting Hong Kong's urban identity, representing Fan Ho's estate and a new generation of local photographers.

galleries.name: AISHONANZUKA
galleries.note: Hong Kong joint venture with Tokyo's NANZUKA, showing Japanese pop, manga-influenced and design-adjacent contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Double Q Gallery
galleries.note: Unusual programme connecting Central and Eastern European artists with Asian audiences through curated, research-led exhibitions.

galleries.name: MOU PROJECTS
galleries.note: Young gallery with an international emerging roster and strong presence at Asian fairs since 2020.

galleries.name: JPS Gallery
galleries.note: Tokyo-rooted gallery popular for contemporary pop, urban and figurative artists with a strong young collector following.

galleries.name: Opera Gallery
galleries.note: International chain gallery with a long-standing Hong Kong presence selling modern masters alongside blue-chip contemporary names.

galleries.name: Art Projects Gallery
galleries.note: Boutique gallery in the Wong Chuk Hang cluster with an abstraction-leaning programme of Asian and European artists.

galleries.name: Galerie Koo
galleries.address_hint: Kwai Bo Industrial Building, 40 Wong Chuk Hang Road
galleries.note: Small gallery showing contemporary ink, painting and ceramics by Chinese and Hong Kong artists in the southside district.

galleries.name: Mine Project
galleries.note: Emerging-artist gallery known for conceptually driven solo presentations by young Chinese and international artists.

galleries.name: f22 foto space
galleries.note: Photography-dedicated space presenting international masters and Hong Kong photographers with well-produced exhibitions and books.

galleries.name: La Galerie Paris 1839
galleries.note: French-founded photography gallery on Hollywood Road, a consistent venue for documentary and fine-art photography in the city.

galleries.name: Floating Projects
galleries.address_hint: 8/F Sing Teck Factory Building, 44 Wong Chuk Hang Road
galleries.note: Artist-run collective space founded by Linda Lai; a laboratory for experimental media, sound and research-based practice.

galleries.name: Current Plans
galleries.note: Independent, artist-led space in Sham Shui Po known for discursive programmes, sound events and support of very young practitioners.

galleries.name: C&G Artpartment
galleries.note: Artist-run space by Clara Cheung and Gum Cheng, long a platform for socially and politically engaged Hong Kong art and art education.

galleries.name: Jockey Club Creative Arts Centre (JCCAC)
galleries.note: Converted factory housing scores of artist studios and public galleries; the largest concentration of working artists in Hong Kong.

galleries.name: Hong Kong Visual Arts Centre
galleries.note: Government studio and exhibition facility in Hong Kong Park that has trained and shown generations of local sculptors, printmakers and ceramicists.

galleries.name: Lumenvisum
galleries.note: Non-profit photography centre running exhibitions, courses and publications that sustain Hong Kong's photographic community.

galleries.name: Hong Kong Open Printshop
galleries.note: Open-access print studio and gallery, the hub of contemporary printmaking and artist-book culture in the city.

galleries.name: The Shophouse
galleries.note: Heritage tong lau converted into a multi-floor art space with a curated, community-minded programme of local and international shows.

galleries.name: Tomorrow Maybe
galleries.note: Hotel-hosted non-commercial space that gave many emerging Hong Kong artists and curators early exhibition opportunities.

galleries.name: Present Projects
galleries.note: Independent Kowloon space focused on photography, publishing and cross-disciplinary projects by younger practitioners.

galleries.name: openground
galleries.note: Design- and publishing-oriented space whose exhibitions and talks helped make Tai Nan Street a creative district.

galleries.name: Parallel Space
galleries.note: Small independent venue for photography, zines and experimental shows within the Sham Shui Po creative cluster.

galleries.name: Hidden Space
galleries.note: Artist-run industrial-building space supporting experimental installation and performance outside the commercial districts.

galleries.name: Wure Area
galleries.note: Artist-run space in a Kowloon East factory building known for raw, low-budget experimental exhibitions and gatherings.

galleries.name: soundpocket
galleries.note: Sound-art organisation running residencies, listening projects and exhibitions that have shaped Hong Kong's sonic art discourse.

galleries.name: Rooftop Institute
galleries.note: Art-education non-profit connecting Hong Kong with Southeast and East Asian artists through exchange programmes and exhibitions.

galleries.name: Belowground
galleries.address_hint: Basement, Landmark Atrium, 15 Queen's Road Central
galleries.note: Retail-adjacent underground project space bringing experimental installations and street-culture-inflected art to a mass Central audience.
